last.verdict: MetLife posted its best-ever quarterly profit per share, but a 49% jump in volatile investment income did much of the work.

takeaways.label: Record, but investment-aided
takeaways.text: Adjusted earnings per share rose 22% to $2.85 excluding one-time items, a company record. Variable investment income, which swings with markets, jumped 49% to $720 million.

takeaways.label: Broad underlying growth
takeaways.text: Premiums and fees excluding pension deals grew 8% to $13.5 billion, with growth in all six segments. Group Benefits earnings rose 15% on favorable claims. Return on equity was 19.6%.

takeaways.label: Patchy spots
takeaways.text: Asia sales fell 6% against a strong year-ago quarter. Latin America earnings excluding one-time items fell 5% on a constant-currency basis, as lower investment returns offset growth.

takeaways.label: Book value split
takeaways.text: Book value per share fell 22% to $30.73, while the adjusted measure, which strips out market swings, rose 5% to $59.41. About $1 billion went back to shareholders.

history.verdict: Investors cheered a clear profit beat driven by better insurance claims results.

reasons.label: Earnings beat
reasons.text: Adjusted earnings of $2.43 per share topped analyst estimates of about $2.29.

reasons.label: Better claims results
reasons.text: Group Benefits profit jumped 25% to $503 million on favorable underwriting and volume growth.

reasons.label: Broad growth, high returns
reasons.text: Every segment grew; return on equity hit 17% for a second straight quarter.
